item: Basis: the Family Code articles on custody (definition and conditions of the custodian, order of custodians, grounds of forfeiture, return of the right, the child's interest as the governing criterion), as amended by Ordinance 05-02.

Prove the earlier judgment that awarded custody to the defendant (copy of the judgment, its date, whether it became final, its service) and that the ground relied on arose after it (new fact), otherwise res judicata may be raised.

Ground 1: marriage of the female custodian to a man who is not a mahram relative of the child: prove the marriage (marriage certificate / civil status extract) and its date; check that the husband is not a mahram relative.
Ground 2: renunciation of custody by the custodian: prove it (written declaration, court record); check the rule that renunciation is accepted only if not contrary to the child's interest.

Ground 3: the custodian no longer meets the conditions of custody (capacity to care for, educate, protect the child's health and morals): prove the specific failing; recall that the custodian woman's work is not by itself a ground of forfeiture; the child's interest must be weighed.

Ground 4: the person entitled did not claim custody for more than one year without excuse: check how the one-year period is counted, from what event, and whether an excuse exists; this is a ground of forfeiture of the right, not a procedural time limit on this claim.
Ground 5: the custodian settled or wants to settle in a foreign country: the judge decides to maintain or forfeit custody, considering the child's interest.
Grandmother or aunt custodian living with the child's mother remarried to a non-mahram: separate forfeiture ground; check whether it is in the store.
Return of custody: when the cause of forfeiture ceases and it was not voluntary, the right returns; check whether the defendant can raise this.

Plaintiff's own standing: check the order of persons entitled to custody (mother, father, maternal grandmother, paternal grandmother, maternal aunt, paternal aunt, nearest relatives) and that the plaintiff is fit to hold custody; the transfer goes to the person the judge finds in the child's interest, not automatically to the plaintiff.

Age of the child: custody of a boy ends at 10 (extendable to 16 if the custodian is a mother who has not remarried), of a girl at marriage age; if the child is beyond custody age the claim has no object.

Burden of proof: the plaintiff proves the ground of forfeiture and the earlier judgment (general rule on proof of the claimant); means of proof in family matters are free; the judge may order a social inquiry or hear the child.

Guardianship (wilaya) request: father is guardian, mother after his death or in specified cases; on divorce the judge grants guardianship to the parent awarded custody; check the article and whether the request is accessory to the transfer.
Competent section: family affairs section of the tribunal (CPCA family matters chapter); custody listed among its matters; import court-sections module.

Territorial jurisdiction: in custody, visitation and maintenance matters, the court of the place where custody is exercised (or the residence of the child); check whether the rule is of public order; import territorial-jurisdiction module.
Public prosecutor is a principal party in family code matters: check the requirement to involve the public prosecution and the consequence of failing to do so.
Reconciliation attempt: required in divorce matters only; check whether any conciliation is required before a custody claim (probably not); import conciliation-mediation for the optional mediation.
No formal notice is required before a custody forfeiture claim; check the formal-notice module confirms none applies.
No limitation period on the claim itself: custody is a continuing status tied to the child's interest; check periods module for any general rule; do not invent a deadline.
Appeal: judgments on custody are open to appeal (unlike the divorce pronouncement itself); check the article.
Urgent measures: the judge may order provisional measures on custody and visitation during proceedings (summary/urgent jurisdiction of the family section president); check the article.
Provisional execution: custody, maintenance and housing judgments may carry provisional execution as of right in family matters; check the CPCA article; import accessory-requests.

Required documents: the earlier custody judgment, the child's birth certificate, family record book, proof of the ground (marriage certificate of the custodian, renunciation, report, residence abroad evidence), plaintiff's identity and residence.
Petition formal elements, fees and standing: import petition-formal-elements.
When granting custody the judge must rule on visitation rights; a transfer judgment should address visitation for the former custodian.
Housing for the custodian: on divorce the father must provide housing for the custodian or pay rent; a transfer may affect who keeps the marital home.

Boundaries: initial custody award in the divorce judgment (not this claim); a mere visitation dispute (visitation claim); enforcement of an existing judgment / non-representation of a child (criminal offence of failing to hand over a child, Penal Code); kafala of an abandoned child (different regime); authorisation for a child to travel abroad; maintenance for children.
Ordinary-court exits: none expected (pure family matter); check ordinary-court-exits for a criminal case on same facts (e.g. abuse) which may suspend the civil case.
Foreign element: if the custodian or child is abroad, check international jurisdiction of Algerian courts and conflict rules; service abroad.

Amendments: Ordinance 05-02 of 27 February 2005 rewrote custody articles (order of custodians, father moved to second place, work of woman not a ground, settlement abroad article); check the store carries the amended text.
What is the legal basis for forfeiting custody (إسقاط الحضانة) and for transferring it to another holder, in the Family Code?
Which conditions must a custodian satisfy (guardianship of the child's religion, upbringing, health, ability to protect), and which of them is lacking here?
Who is entitled to custody in order (mother, father, maternal grandmother, etc.), and is the plaintiff within that order or the guardian?
Does the remarriage of the custodian with a non-relative of the child forfeit custody, and are there exceptions (the judge's discretion about the child's interest)?
Does renunciation of custody by the custodian end it, and may the custodian go back on it?
Does failure to claim custody for more than a year without excuse forfeit the right? Where does the year start and who may raise it?
What is the effect of the custodian settling abroad or wishing to settle abroad, and what does the judge weigh?
Is there a prior judgment awarding custody (date, court, finality) and has it become final or is it still under appeal?
Is the claim an independent action or a request that must be made in an existing divorce case?
Which court section hears it (family section) and what happens when the court has no sections or the case goes to the wrong section?
Which court by place: the place where custody is exercised, or the custodian's domicile? What does the Code of Civil Procedure provide?
Is the territorial rule of public order?
Must a conciliation attempt precede the claim, and is a record of non-conciliation needed?
Is a formal notice to the defendant required before filing?
Is the public prosecutor a party or to be notified in custody matters?
Is there a limitation or forfeiture period to file, and from what event does it run?
What must be proved, by whom, and by what means (judgment, marriage certificate, social or medical inquiry, witnesses)?
Which documents must be attached to the petition (copy of the earlier judgment, family record book, birth certificate of the child, proof of the custodian's remarriage)?
May the judge order a social inquiry or an expert report and appoint a guardian ad litem for the child?
Which requests can be made with the main request: custody transfer, guardianship, visitation, maintenance, housing?
May the claim include damages, costs, or provisional execution, and which texts support each?
Is the judgment on custody provisionally enforceable by law, and does an appeal suspend it?
What are the mandatory elements of the petition and what does their absence cost?
Does the best interest of the child limit the judge to deciding against the literal conditions of forfeiture?
Which ordinary-court exits are relevant (none expected: administrative or commercial courts, criminal judge)?
Does the claim have to name the child's legal representative and the father or mother as parties?
Is the plaintiff's standing established (father, mother, other relative of the child) and what interest does each have?
